resources.name: LFP Router Fingerprinting Artifacts
quotes: Lightweight FingerPrinting (LFP), a novel lightweight, accurate, and more complete remote vendor fingerprinting methodology and tool (§3).
LFP is publicly available, along with the the derived signatures and classification results from this study to enable reproducibility and future work [3].
references: Taha Albakour, Oliver Gasser, Robert Beverly, and Georgios Smaragdakis. 2023. Illuminating Router Vendor Diversity Within Providers and Along Network Paths (artifacts). https://routerfingerprinting.github.io/.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The paper introduces LFP as its primary methodology and tool for router fingerprinting and provides the artifacts for reproducibility.

resources.name: Censys Universal Internet Dataset
quotes: For this, we acquire a set of addresses from Censys, which are known to reveal vendor information through service banners.
references: Zakir Durumeric, David Adrian, Ariana Mirian, Michael Bailey, and J. Alex Halderman. 2015. A Search Engine Backed by Internet-Wide Scanning. In ACM CCS.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors use a set of addresses from Censys to evaluate the accuracy of LFP by comparing it against known vendor information from service banners.

resources.name: ITDK
quotes: To select target router IPs, we leverage two complementary public router datasets: the RIPE Atlas traceroutes dataset [43] and the ITDK dataset [11].
references: CAIDA. 2021. Macroscopic Internet Topology Data Kit (ITDK). https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/internet-topology-data-kit/.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The ITDK dataset is used as one of the two primary sources for target router IPs to gather signatures and perform router-level analysis.

resources.name: CAIDA|AS Relationships
quotes: Next, we use the CAIDA AS relationship dataset [12] to find AS paths where these vendor homogeneous ASes serve as transit ASes.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The CAIDA AS relationship dataset is used to identify AS paths for the informed routing case study.

resources.name: MIDAR
quotes: This complementary dataset contains router alias sets (excluding singletons) inferred via MIDAR [29] and iffinder measurements.
alias resolution tools such as MIDAR [29] and Ally [47] use monotonic IPID counters to infer aliases
references: K. Keys, Y. Hyun, M. Luckie, and k claffy. 2013. Internet-Scale IPv4 Alias Resolution with MIDAR. IEEE/ACM Trans. Networking 21, 2 (2013).
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: MIDAR is mentioned as a tool used to infer the alias sets within the ITDK dataset and as an example of IPID-based fingerprinting in related work.
